key_insight: Foundational-NCA uses just 211,000 parameters to adapt to medical image segmentation tasks through genetic prompting without retraining.
clinical_relevance: Its compact size could support segmentation tools in resource-limited healthcare settings, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Combines gradient-based learning with genetic optimization in a latent task space.
Uses a compact task vector to guide segmentation predictions.
evidence_signal: On TotalSegmentator, evaluation covered 15 trained and 6 unseen segmentation tasks, with average Dice scores of 84.5% and 60.4%, respectively.
watch_item: Lower performance on unseen tasks warrants further validation before deployment, and parameter count alone does not establish runtime efficiency.
paper_title: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata
